context: Associative unital division ring, not necessarily commutative
editorial_note: The independent ProofWiki source explicitly specifies additive-group, associative-multiplication, distributivity, 1≠0, and two-sided inverse laws. No commutativity of scalar multiplication is assumed. This is an associative skew field, not the Encyclopedia of Mathematics broader nonassociative usage of the term division ring. Do not conflate a division ring with an arbitrary associative unital ring or a commutative field. It can serve as the scalar ring for either left or right unitary modules. Source carries bibliography to textbooks but their pages were not read. Page sections: Definition 1, Definition 2, Also known as
text: A division ring D is a nonzero associative unital ring whose nonzero elements form a group under multiplication. Its addition is an abelian group, multiplication distributes over addition on both sides, and every nonzero element has a two-sided multiplicative inverse.

context: Real-valued multiplicative norm on an associative division ring
editorial_note: ProofWiki gives positive definiteness, exact multiplicativity, and the triangle inequality, with no commutativity requirement on D. For nonzero D, |1|=1, |−1|=1 and |a^{-1}|=|a|^{-1} follow; these are consequences, not additional independent axioms. Contrast the source's norm-on-arbitrary-ring entry, which only imposes submultiplicativity and explicitly lacks bibliography. The value |·|_D is a scalar multiplicative norm/absolute value, NOT the field extension norm N_{L/K} defined by a determinant. The ProofWiki source lists Gouvea/Katok under normed fields, so the noncommutative extension remains individually mathematically reasoned rather than bibliographically confirmed from those books. Page sections: Definition, Notes, Sources
text: Let D be an associative division ring. A multiplicative norm is a map |·|_D:D→ℝ_{≥0} satisfying |a|_D=0 iff a=0, |ab|_D=|a|_D|b|_D for all a,b∈D, and |a+b|_D≤|a|_D+|b|_D for all a,b∈D.

context: Associative division ring equipped with a specified multiplicative real-valued norm
editorial_note: This ProofWiki page explicitly defines a normed division ring by equipping a division ring with a norm, but flags the page as lacking bibliographic source citations. The norm's actual multiplicative axioms are stated on the separately read ProofWiki Definition:Norm on Division Ring page, and the associative division ring laws on Definition:Division Ring. Therefore the pair definition is mathematically source-cross-checked within ProofWiki, not claimed independently corroborated by an inaccessible cited textbook. Do not confuse this structure with a generic normed ring using merely |ab|≤|a||b|, nor with a Banach division algebra, which adds completeness. Editorial evidence quality is lower until a separate rigorous reference confirms this exact terminology. Page sections: Definition, Sources
text: A normed division ring is a pair (D,|·|_D), where D is an associative unital division ring and |·|_D:D→ℝ_{≥0} is a specified multiplicative norm satisfying positive definiteness and the triangle inequality.

context: Unital left vector space over an associative division ring
editorial_note: ProofWiki individually lists left vector spaces as unital left modules over division rings and gives explicitly oriented action D×V→V, associativity (ab)v=a(bv), both distributivity laws and the unity condition. The noncommutative division ring case must not be identified with a right D-vector space merely by reversing notation; a right action can instead arise through the opposite ring. Existing independently screened unital left modules over associative unital rings provide a mathematical superclass without making the scalar division ring commutative. In the source's generic normed vector-space axiom |av|, the scalar multiplication is left-oriented. Page sections: Definition 1, Definition 2, Left vs Right Vector Space
text: For an associative division ring D, a left D-vector space is an abelian group (V,+) with scalar action D×V→V, (a,v)↦av, satisfying a(v+w)=av+aw, (a+b)v=av+bv, (ab)v=a(bv), and 1_Dv=v.

context: Unital right vector space over an associative division ring
editorial_note: ProofWiki independently distinguishes right vector spaces from left vector spaces in noncommutative division-ring settings; the right action is V×D→V and associativity is (va)b=v(ab). The existing separately screened unital right module over an associative ring is the appropriate structural superclass. The norm-on-vector-space source spells |av| (left scalar action); any right scalar norm version must use |va| and receive separate source/meaning screening rather than declaring both conventions literally identical. The right-space page names an Artin/Milgram reference, but its book content was not separately accessed. Page sections: Definition 1, Definition 2, Left vs Right Vector Space, Sources
text: For an associative division ring D, a right D-vector space is an abelian group (V,+) with scalar action V×D→V, (v,a)↦va, satisfying (v+w)a=va+wa, v(a+b)=va+vb, (va)b=v(ab), and v1_D=v.
